record.question: Which of the following is definitely true in the context of the passage?
options: Profit maximization directly proportional to ethical behaviour.
People having ethical behaviour always in loss at their working place.
Corporate culture does not understand business behaviour.
record.explanation: Checked the printed page 3 of '1. Middle School HeadMaster(LDE)Paper-I.pdf' (LDE, Oct 2019, Paper I) and the shared passage for Q3-12: only the first option survives the passage. It is contradicted that ethical people are always at a loss, since the passage says ethical behaviour and corporate social responsibility 'can bring significant benefits to a business' - attracting customers 'thereby boosting sales and profits', raising productivity and keeping share price high - and it is also contradicted that corporate culture does not understand business behaviour, since business ethics 'examines ethical principles and moral or ethical problems that arise in a business environment' and 'applies to all aspects of business conduct'. That rules out the 'both (b) & (c)' option, leaving the profit-ethics link as the only statement the passage supports (ethical behaviour is tied to higher sales/profits rather than to losses). Confidence is only medium because 'directly proportional' overstates the passage's hedged 'can/may bring significant benefits', and the passage also notes that behaving ethically 'may involve rejecting the route that would lead to the biggest short-term profit', so the stem's 'definitely true' framing is loose.
